minutes.headline: Select Board heard members' ARPA rankings, with no votes; PFAS well testing sent to Board of Health; accountant appointed.
minutes.summary: The board heard each member's ranking of uncommitted ARPA requests, with votes deferred to August 15. Discussion centered on private-well PFAS testing and questions for the Board of Health. The board also made appointments, heard the town manager's report and capital project updates, approved a water commitment, and appointed an interim finance director/town accountant after executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board appointed an interim finance director/town accountant after executive session.
Members presented their rankings of uncommitted ARPA requests; no votes were taken, and a compiled common ranking is due August 15.
The board decided to invite the Board of Health to a future discussion of PFAS testing for private wells before any decision.
The board approved the first quarter FY24 water commitment and made appointments, including election workers and a Monty Tech term correction.
The town manager said the town hall roof repair would be phased, with any shortfall covered from the operating budget or by returning to Town Meeting.

why_it_matters: No ARPA money was committed at this meeting, so how the remaining uncommitted funds are used is still open and will turn on the August 15 discussion.
A roof shortfall could be met from the operating budget or by a new Town Meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on town hall roof funding.
Whether the town helps private-well owners test for PFAS is waiting on the Board of Health's input.
watch_next: August 15 meeting: ARPA priorities discussed from a compiled common ranking, with votes deferred to that date.
Whether the August 8 meeting is cancelled, to be decided by Thursday noon.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary:
The two records agree on four of the five votes, plus the abatement refund, LED, water commitment and warrant figures. They differ on the election workers vote, the Town Hall roof figure, and several items in only one record.
A reader should know that our minutes show an election workers appointment vote and several decisions (cancelling Aug 8, April 25 minutes, PFAS) that the official minutes omit, while the official minutes show the interim finance director appointment that ours lacks.
